name: Planning exercise around your hair
what_people_do: Change hairstyle for exercise or skip workouts to protect a style that took hours and money.
why_they_say_it_works: Sweat and water ruin straightened or braided styles; washing and restyling takes too long.

documented_by.source: Hall RR et al 2013, JAMA Dermatol, PMID 23682367
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Winston-Salem, 103 African American women: 50% modified their style to accommodate exercise and 37.9% sometimes avoided exercise because of hair.

documented_by.source: Gathers RC, Mahan MG 2014, J Clin Aesthet Dermatol, PMID 25276273
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Detroit church survey, 200 women: 45% avoided exercise because of hair concerns; 22% felt hair impeded healthy weight.

evidence.finding: Those who exercised less because of hair were 2.9 times less likely to exceed 150 min a week (CI 0.9 to 9.4, P=0.08), not significant.

source.name: Hall RR et al 2013, JAMA Dermatol, PMID 23682367

harm_note: The practice protects the style at a cost to exercise; low-manipulation styles and swim caps are the usual compromise.
gaps: Church-based convenience samples; association not causation.
